extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and patent practitioners interested in automated patent claim generation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of large language models' ability to generate high-quality patent claims from patent texts, using automatic and human (patent-expert) assessments of claim quality dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of inventions' features
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tuning can enhance the completeness of inventions' features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether generated claims include all salient technical features of the invention as described in the specification/description. The paper reports fine-tuning improves this dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses how clearly the claim expresses the invention's concepts and boundaries. In human evaluations GPT-4 scored better on conceptual clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature linkage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how well individual claim features are connected/related within the claim (logical linkage among elements) and across dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: GPT-4 demonstrates the best performance in comprehensive human evaluations by patent experts, with better feature coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree to which claims cover the set of invention features present in the description; used by patent experts during comprehensive evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: GPT-4 demonstrates the best performance ... with better ... technical coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates internal technical consistency of the claim language and whether the claim's technical statements make sense together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of first independent claims vs dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs can produce high-quality first independent claims, but their performances markedly decrease for subsequent dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate evaluation of independent claim quality (often stronger) and dependent claim generation (linking back to and properly narrowing independent claims); highlights model weaknesses on dependent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal robustness / ability to pass rigorous patent scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive revision and modification are still necessary to pass rigorous patent scrutiny and ensure legal robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond surface quality metrics, claims must satisfy legal/office examination standards; autogenerated claims typically require expert revision to be legally robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input source for claim generation (description vs abstract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generating claims based on patent descriptions outperforms previous research relying on abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a procedural/quality criterion: using the full patent description as the input context produces higher-quality claims than using only abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection: patent-specific LLMs vs general LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Current patent-specific LLMs perform much worse than state-of-the-art general LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for evaluating/generated claims: choice of model architecture/training matters; off-the-shelf general LLMs (e.g., GPT-4) may outperform smaller or domain-specialized models in claim quality metrics used by experts.
